chunks: My father narrated to us, may God be pleased with him, who said: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated to us, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali al-Washsha', from Ar-Rida (peace be upon him) who said: I heard him say,

My father (peace be upon him) said: Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) said: Indeed, God, the Mighty and Exalted, said, 'O Noah! He is not of your family, for he was opposed to him, and He considered those who followed him to be of his family.'

Al-Washsha' said: How do people recite this verse regarding the son of Noah? I said: People recite it in two ways: 'Inna-hu 'amalu ghayr salih' (He is a deed of non-righteousness) and 'Inna-hu 'amila ghayr salih' (He did a deed of non-righteousness).
He (peace be upon him) said: They are lying. He was indeed his son. However, God, the Mighty and Exalted, distanced him from him when he opposed him in his religion.
ai.seo_question: Why is Noah's son said to not be of his family in the Quran?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Saduq records this narration from Imam al-Rida to resolve the exegetical debate regarding Noah's son, affirming that while the son was biologically Noah's, he was spiritually excluded from the 'family' (ahl) due to his divergence in faith (din). This highlights the Shia principle that spiritual allegiance and adherence to divine command take precedence over mere biological lineage, a concept central to the understanding of the Ahl al-Bayt's status.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 32-3 (The author of the book narrated) my father - may God be pleased with him - narrated that Sa’d ibn Abdullah quoted on the authority of Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa that Al-Hassan ibn Ali al-Washsha’ said that he had heard Ar-Ridha’ (a.s.) say,

“My father (a.s.) narrated that Abu Abdullah (a.s.) said that the Honorable the Exalted God told Noah, ‘…O Noah! He is not of thy family…’ The reason for this was that Noah’s son was opposed to Noah. God considered those who followed Noah (a.s.) to be of his family.”

Al-Washsha’ said that the Imam (a.s.) asked him, “How is this verse about Noah’s son recited?” Al-Washsha’ answered, “The people recite it in two different ways one form of which implies that he was not Noah’s son.”
The Imam (a.s.) said, “No, they are liars. He was Noah’s son. However, the Honorable the Exalted God denounced him from being Noah’s son due to his opposition to Noah’s religion.”
